study type: Mixed-methods study with secondary data analysis (interrupted time series analysis) and key informant interviews.
cohort: The study analyzed 18 healthcare service indicators from the Zimbabwe District Health Information Systems 2 (DHIS2) and collected data from key informant interviews.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic negatively impacted health service delivery in Zimbabwe, causing increased disruptions of critical healthcare services, a decline in service usage, and a rise in maternal and child mortality cases and caesarean sections.
mod_finding: The rise in caesarean sections could be directly linked to the decline in service delivery during the pandemic.
